newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude market deadly quiet, eastern arb widen.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude market deadly quiet, eastern arb widen.

text.p: The North Sea crude market was eerily quiet on Wednesday morning, with action desperately thin on both the paper and physical markets.
"It's absolutely dead. I haven't heard anything done at all," said one trader.
No trades were reported on Brent intermonth spreads, but June/July firmed fractionally in morning discussion to -13/-11 cents, having traded twice at -16 cents in the U.S. aftermarket.

A wide bid/ask range on CFDs failed to narrow over the course of the morning, with next week's dates (May 12-16) talked weaker at June Brent -45/-35 cents by midday. The following week was pegged at -37/-30 cents.
Outright June Brent was trading 11 cents up at $18.18 a barrel at 1120 GMT, off a high of $18.28 cents.

The market was boosted by U.S. gasoline inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which showed record "implied demand" levels for last week, although traders were awaiting confirmation from U.S. government figures to be released this afternoon.
The physical North Sea market was thinly talked with wet Brent notionally assessed slightly weaker than Tuesday's traded levels of June Brent -28 cents.
No full Brent cargoes were nominated loading dates on Wednesday according to the May schedule.
A steady Brent market coupled with a firmer Dubai intermonth spreads led to a sharp narrowing of the Brent/Dubai market, keeping the West-to East arbitrage wide open.
The Dubai June/July intermonth spread climbed to +35/+50, squeezing the July Brent/Dubai spread to the +75/+90 range, after deals were done at over +$1.00 on Tuesday.
